message.content:
### Killing **Visual Studio Code** (`code.exe`) with *Task‑Kill*

On Windows you can force‑terminate an application (or its children) directly from the Command Prompt or PowerShell with the built‑in `taskkill` utility.

> **Syntax**

```cmd
taskkill [options] [/PID <process_id>|/IM <image_name>] ...
```

#### Quick one‑liner

If you simply want to close every instance of VS Code running under your account:

```powershell
taskkill /IM code.exe /F
```

* `/IM code.exe` – target the executable name  
* `/F`          – force termination (no graceful shutdown)

---

#### Terminate only the current user’s VS Code windows

Sometimes other users may have launched VS Code; add `/FI` filters:

```powershell
taskkill /IM code.exe /F /FI "USERNAME eq %username%"
```

---

#### Kill VS Code plus all spawned child processes

VS Code often spawns helper processes (`node`, extensions, debuggers). If those keep hanging after the main window closes, add `/T`:

```powershell
taskkill /IM code.exe /F /T
```

This will recursively terminate the entire tree rooted at each matching `code.exe`.

---

#### Verify before killing

To see which `code.exe` instances exist (and their PIDs):

```powershell
tasklist /FI "IMAGENAME eq code.exe"
```

Then pick the PID(s) you wish to end:

```powershell
taskkill /PID 12345 /F   # replace 12345 with actual PID
```

---

#### Common gotchas & tips

| Issue | Fix |
|-------|-----|
| “Access denied” error | Run the console as Administrator or ensure you’re terminating only your own processes. |
| VS Code still appears frozen | Some extension workers may survive; try adding `/T` to kill descendants. |
| You accidentally killed unrelated apps | Double‑check the image name (`code.exe`). A typo could match another program. |

---

#### Example workflow

1. **Open PowerShell** (right‑click → “Run as administrator” if necessary).
2. List VS Code processes:
    ```powershell
    tasklist /FI "IMAGENAME eq code.exe"
    ```
3. Forcefully stop them:
    ```powershell
    taskkill /IM code.exe /F /T
    ```

That’s it—your VS Code session should disappear immediately. Remember that this bypasses normal cleanup hooks, so unsaved work may be lost. Use it when the IDE becomes unresponsive but otherwise avoid frequent forced kills.
